expected: A converge preview evaluates every lane (INTEGRATED, READY, the pending BLOCKED, NOT_READY and WAITING, the failing MISSING_BRANCH, DIRTY, IN_PROGRESS, NO_MERGE_BASE, OUT_OF_LANE, SHARED_CHANGE, MOVED, CLAIM_DRIFT and STALE_PLAN, and the hint PREDICTED_CONFLICT); a failing finding stops the whole command so that a ready lane that is inconsistent is never merged around, and the readiness is READY, PARTIAL or BLOCKED with the next command and the remedy of every failed gate.

--converge --apply is the user's acceptance of the recorded lane heads it puts in its report: it re-surveys, stops when a lane head, the target tip or the revision differs from the earlier preview, creates agent/<set>/integration with a plain git switch -c from the current target tip in the invoking worktree, merges each READY lane's recorded head with git merge --no-ff in dependency order, records each with set-update, and runs the repository checks before any land.

A conflict lists the unmerged paths, runs git merge --abort and stops; it is never resolved with ours, theirs or by hand, the completed merges stay on the integration branch only, and the report names the lane, the files, the error text and the integration start SHA.

--land adds one git merge --ff-only of the integration branch into the target, only while every lane is integrated and the target still sits at the integration start SHA (otherwise LAND_REFUSED with both SHAs and nothing else); --release prints the final checklist and then removes only the claims and the record.

The hard stops: never push, fetch, force, delete a branch or a worktree, touch main, use override, arm, disarm or install, edit .git/magos or write the record other than through set-plan, set-update and set-release, rebase, squash, cherry-pick, reset, resolve a conflict with ours or theirs, write inside a lane worktree, or merge anything but a recorded lane head; every git and guard command is an argument list.

Every gate, finding, guard exit code and stop of an apply is followed by its remedy, which the command never performs; a rerun after an interruption resumes on the same integration branch and skips the lanes that are already integrated.

**Pending** findings leave the lane out of this run and stop nothing; a **failing** finding stops the whole command, in the preview as a failed gate, so a ready lane that is inconsistent is never merged around.
BLOCKED             pending   the recorded state is blocked
WAITING             pending   a dependency is neither INTEGRATED nor READY in this run
MISSING_BRANCH      failing   branch_exists is false
NO_MERGE_BASE       failing   the branch exists and changed is null
OUT_OF_LANE         failing   out_of_lane is not empty (the files are listed)

### Converge preview (`--converge [--include-active]`, read-only)

4. **Readiness**: `READY` when no gate fails and every lane is `READY` or `INTEGRATED`: one run of the next command merges all of them, and `--land` can follow in the same run. `PARTIAL` when no gate fails but some lane is pending: the next command merges the `READY` lanes and the report lists what each pending lane needs. `BLOCKED` when a gate fails.
`--land` is only suggested in words, never added to the line.
### Converge apply (`--converge --apply [--include-active] [--land] [--expect-revision <n>]`)

- **Convergence.** `--converge --apply` is the user's acceptance of the lane heads listed in the plan that the run records and puts in its report, or in a converge preview of the same set earlier in this conversation, and with `--land` of one fast-forward of `<branch>` to the integration branch. It permits no write to any branch except the integration branch and, with `--land`, the target, and never to `main`.
2. **Include active lanes** (only with `--include-active`): for each such lane run `<guard> set-update --set <set> --expect-revision <rev> --lane <id> --state ready --head '<tip>'`
run `git -C <top> switch -c 'agent/<set>/integration' '<target sha>'` (the CURRENT target tip; that SHA is the integration start SHA).

`git -C <top> merge --no-ff -m 'Merge lane <id> of plan <set> into agent/<set>/integration' '<recorded head>'`. Never `--no-verify`, `-X ours`, `-X theirs`, `--allow-unrelated-histories`, squash or rebase.
5. Record it: `<guard> set-update --set <set> --expect-revision <rev> --lane <id> --state integrated --head '<recorded head>' --integration 'agent/<set>/integration'`.

On a conflict list the unmerged paths (`git -C <top> diff --name-only --diff-filter=U`), run `git -C <top> merge --abort`, and stop; never resolve it with ours or theirs, and never by hand. Completed merges stay on the integration branch only.

5. **Validate** with the repository normal checks in the invoking worktree, on the integration branch, once at least one lane was merged or recorded, or `--land` was typed. A failed check stops the run before any land
6. **Land** (only with `--land`, after step 5 did not fail)

`git -C <top> merge --ff-only '<integration tip sha>'`, and confirm that `git rev-parse refs/heads/<target>` equals that SHA. When a condition fails, report `LAND_REFUSED` with the failed condition and both SHAs and do nothing else (**Remedies**); the invoking worktree stays on the integration branch.
A rerun after an interruption or a conflict starts from a fresh survey and resumes on the same integration branch: lanes already `integrated` are skipped

2. Run `<guard> set-release --set <set> --reason integrated`. Exit 0 removes the lane claims, the integration claim and the record and appends to the guard's audit log; exit 16 means a lane is not integrated, is not yet in the target or has a dirty worktree, and the guard names it (**Remedies**).
3. Report the released claims (`released`), and that the lane branches, their worktrees and the integration branch are not touched
| apply stopped by a conflict | the report names the lane, the files, the error text and the integration start SHA; completed merges stay on the integration branch and their lanes stay `integrated`.
| apply stopped because a `set-update` failed after a merge |

| apply stopped by a failed check | fix what it names, on the integration branch by a commit of your own or in the lane (then record the lane `ready` again), then rerun; the check ran on the merged result; completed merges stay and nothing was landed |
| `LAND_REFUSED`: the target moved since the integration start SHA
| creation stopped: a lane's worktree path or branch exists

`/GitPlan <set> --converge --apply` is the user's acceptance of the recorded lane heads: it merges them in dependency order into `agent/<set>/integration` only (created with `git switch -c` from the current target tip; a denial of that creation is quoted and stops the run), records each with `set-update`, stops on a conflict, runs the repository's normal checks, and with `--land` makes one `--ff-only` merge of that branch into `<branch>` while `<branch>` still sits at the integration start; `--release` removes the claims and the record through `set-release`.

It never pushes, force-pushes, deletes a branch or worktree, touches `main`, uses `override`, rebases, squashes, or resolves a conflict by ours/theirs, and runs every git and guard command as an argument list. See `references/commands.md` section 8.
